  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           Compare and contrast supervised and unsupervised learning. Provide examples of real-  
  world tasks that fall under each category and discuss how machine learning techniques  
  (5)

  A)  
  B)      Evaluate the ethical implications of using ensemble learning methods such as bagging  
  and boosting in decision-making systems. Discuss potential issues related to fairness,      (5)  
  transparency, and accountability, and propose strategies for addressing these concerns.  
  
  2)           Compare the robustness of K-Means clustering, the EM algorithm, and Hierarchical  
  clustering in handling overlapping clusters and noisy data. Which method is most  
  resilient in scenarios with high variance in cluster density, and why? Provide examples     (5)  
  A)      of application scenarios where each method might excel or struggle.  
  
  B)      Make use of strategies for tuning kernel parameters, such as the degree of polynomial  
  kernels or the bandwidth of Gaussian RBF kernels, to optimize SVM model  
  performance? How do these parameter choices impact model robustness and                     (5)  
  generalization across different datasets.  
  
  3)           Evaluate the main steps of the K-means clustering algorithm, examining processes such  
  as initialization, cluster assignment, and centroid updating.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      Compare parametric and non-parametric models in terms of their assumptions,  
  flexibility, and scalability in classification and regression tasks. Provide examples where  
  a parametric model like logistic regression might outperform a non-parametric model,        (5)  
  and vice versa. Discuss the trade-offs involved in terms of model interpretability and  
  generalization.  
  
  4)           The design of the fitness function in a genetic algorithm significantly impacts the  
  algorithm's performance. Discuss how a poorly designed fitness function can lead to  
  suboptimal solutions or convergence to local minima. How can knowledge from neural          (5)  
  A)      network loss functions be applied to improve fitness function design in genetic  
  algorithms  
  
  B)      Discuss the role of different distance metrics (e.g., Euclidean, Manhattan, Minkowski) in (5)  
  the K-NN algorithm. How does the choice of distance metric affect K-NN's
